title: Conscience Bay–Little Bay: Setalcott Stewardship
summary: A public wetland landscape where Setalcott leaders connect ancestral ties to present-day conservation and restoration.
address_label: Dyke Road near North Road, Setauket, NY
map_geometry_source: Approximate public wetland access area west of Dyke Road, north of North Road, matched to NYSDEC map p.1 and OpenStreetMap road geometry; not a surveyed parking-space coordinate.
why_this_matters: Setalcott history continues through decisions about water, habitat and public access. This place connects community leadership with the long-term care of ancestral land.
history_title: A Living Connection to Ancestral Waters
history_content:
On April 24, 2025, Setalcott leaders joined DEC and community partners at the improved wetland area. Helen Sells, Robert “Silver Wolf” Thompson and youth chair A’riel “Thundering Sparrow” Hart spoke. The gathering made contemporary Setalcott care for this landscape visible.1

DEC credits the Nation among the partners who helped the project. The agency’s acquisitions along Dyke Road protected wetlands and adjoining uplands while adding public access.2

Restoration led by the Nation

The 2025 Long Island Sound Community Impact Fund awarded the Setalcott Nation $90,700 for its Historical Stewardship Restoration Project. Its plan includes native planting at Conscience Bay, study of whether an oyster hatchery is feasible, and kelp farming at Poquott. The award documents intended work; it does not by itself establish that every element has been completed.3
whereintheworld_content:
The pin gives approximate orientation to the DEC wetland access area on the west side of Dyke Road, north of North Road. Use DEC’s posted entrance and current access map; the marker is not a surveyed parking-space location. Respect adjacent homes and wetland vegetation.4

Public access does not mean permission to gather plants, shellfish or artifacts. Follow posted rules and current DEC guidance.
